paper.title: A Bayesian Approach to Online Planning

settings.name_in_paper: Bayesian Tree Search (sequential discovery of a deterministic decision tree with prior over rewards)
unmapped: Arms are leaf state-action pairs of a deterministic decision tree of depth H with finite action set; each query reveals the deterministic reward of a frontier leaf, and the set of available leaves grows as the tree is expanded
Regret is measured on the root action leading to the queried leaf: sum_t Q_0(s_0,A*) - Q_0(s_0,A_root(z_t))
Rewards r(s,a) in [-R_max, R_max]; tree drawn from a known prior P(T)
settings.definition_quote: Consider a deterministic decision process $\tree$ with an initial (root) state $s_0$, and a finite action set $A$. ... We assume a prior distribution over the rewards, which induces a distribution over the trees ... We consider a sequential and stochastic discovery of the tree that takes place over $T$ iterations ... where at each iteration $t$, a reward for a particular leaf state-action pair $\leaf_t = (s_t,a_t)$ is revealed

symbols.R_max: bound on absolute per-step reward |r(s,a)| <= R_max
symbols.Z_size: number of state-action pairs in the tree |Z|
symbols.Ent_zstar: Shannon entropy of the prior distribution of the optimal leaf z*

conditions: optimal root action unique for every tree in the prior support
posterior sampling noise independent of the past and of A* (technical assumption in proof)
tuning: leaf selection by exact probability matching P(z_t = z | F_t) = P(z_t^* = z | F_t)

source.label: thm:TSTS_regret
source.quote: The regret of the leaf selection rule defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:TS_action_prob} satisfies: $\mathbb{E}\left[\textrm{Regret}(T)\right] \leq \hor R_{max}\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}|\leaves|\ent(\leaf^*)T}.$

results.notes: Bayesian regret over prior on trees, regret measured on the root action. Proof via Russo & Van Roy information ratio bound Gamma_t <= |Z| R_max^2 H^2 / 2. Setting mapping (structured bandit over tree leaves) is approximate; the algorithm is exact Thompson sampling over leaves, efficient implementation only under independent posteriors.
